title: Failed sign-ins against a disabled account, by an address that succeeded elsewhere
sourceData: Microsoft Sentinel Training Lab — disable_accounts_CL, sign_in_adelete_CL, OfficeActivity_CL
summary: Four sign-in attempts against johns@m365x816222.onmicrosoft.com from 175.45.176.99 all failed, because the account is disabled. The same address authenticated successfully 53 times as adelev@m365x816222.onmicrosoft.com in the same period, and that session created an anonymous sharing link on 'Contoso Purchasing Data - Q1.xlsx' before deleting a file. The control worked for this account and for no other.

discriminatingEvidence.question: Did any attempt against this account succeed?
discriminatingEvidence.expected: All 4 attempts are ResultType 50057, 'User account is disabled' — zero successes against johns@

discriminatingEvidence.question: Has that address succeeded against any other identity?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: union withsource=T disable_accounts_CL, sign_in_adelete_CL, OktaV2_CL, OfficeActivity_CL, AzureActivity_CL | where * has '175.45.176.99' | summarize n=count() by T
discriminatingEvidence.expected: Four tables: disable_accounts_CL 4, sign_in_adelete_CL 56, OfficeActivity_CL 176, AzureActivity_CL 1. The address is not confined to the failed attempts

discriminatingEvidence.question: What did it achieve where it did succeed?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: sign_in_adelete_CL | summarize SignIns=count(), Successful=countif(ResultType == 0) by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress
discriminatingEvidence.expected: adelev@m365x816222.onmicrosoft.com, 56 sign-ins from 175.45.176.99 of which 53 succeeded

discriminatingEvidence.question: Did that session do anything destructive?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: OfficeActivity_CL | where ClientIP == '175.45.176.99' | where Operation in ('AnonymousLinkCreated','SharingSet','FileDeleted','PermissionLevelAdded') | project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, SourceFileName | order by TimeGenerated asc
discriminatingEvidence.expected: Permission grants and sharing changes by both johns and adelev, an AnonymousLinkCreated on 'Contoso Purchasing Data - Q1.xlsx', and a FileDeleted

trap: Everything about the alert says close it: four attempts, all failed, against an account that is already disabled. The preventive control did work — for this identity. Scoping the assessment to the alerted account produces a defensible-sounding 'no impact' that misses a confirmed compromise of a second identity by the same address in the same window. The pivot from the account to the address is the entire investigation.
evaluatorNotes: The most important thing this scenario tests is whether a low-severity, all-failed alert gets pivoted on rather than closed. The verdict is easy; the impact is where investigations fail. An assessment returning impact 'none' has answered the narrow question — the attempts failed — and stopped at the boundary of the alert. Note the country field disagrees between tables: disable_accounts_CL labels 175.45.176.99 as KP and sign_in_adelete_CL labels the same address IL, so attribution built on geolocation is reasoning from data the corpus contradicts. Related: adele-signin-compromise, adele-sharepoint-exfiltration.
